prior.note: tests/duelOnline.test.ts:L54-57 now reads watchdogs() when rig.session().duel.interior.tick % 300 === 299. duelRules.ts:L35 confirms that interior.tick is the same tick the authority uses (rules.tick), so each read comes after the pump that reaches tick 299 and before the reset in core.ts:L458-459, which runs after the step that reaches tick 300. L58 asserts windows === floor((T+1)/300), so a pump that skipped tick 299 would fail the test rather than skip a window. The final window is still read at L71. One gap remains: watchdog frames journaled in the boundary pump before its tick runs (expireHeld/drainIngress, core.ts:L471-472) are cleared without being read. That is one pump in every 300, and the finding marked covering it as optional, so it does not keep this open.

tests/duelOnline.test.ts:L76 asserts heldHighWater[seat] > 0 for each seat. Seat 1's held frames can only come from b's client, so a seat-specific held/outbox/ACK regression now fails. L77 requires an applied command overall. The responder's reason for dropping the per-seat applied check (the Helm can fly a round on held input alone, false on four seeds) is sound.

duelProducers.ts:L64 clears s.lost whenever the publication is paused, before the early return on s.pending/done at L65. The new test (tests/duelProducers.test.ts:L111-137 in the diff) puts the presence in flight, then delivers paused, then resume plus the applied result, and expects pauses === []. Without L64 the old early return on s.pending left lost true and the applied result triggered pause('peer-lost') at L60, so the test fails without the fix. Steward behaviour in the running and peer-lost paths is otherwise unchanged.

duelClient.ts:L21-27 now checks publication.tick === snapshot.header.tick and the hash (hashF64 over Float64Array.from(snapshot.values)) after schema parsing and before validateDuelSnapshot. These are the same checks checkedPublication makes (duelStream.ts:L26), and the doc at L19-20 now describes them. The stream client's validatePublication (duelClient.ts:L35) uses it, which also closes minor (a).

verified: core.ts:L458-459: the boundary reset runs after rules.step and publishCompletedState, so frames for tick 299 are still in replay().frames when the test reads at interior.tick % 300 === 299 (tests/duelOnline.test.ts:L56).
tests/helpers/onlineDuel.ts:L51: rig.tick() advances the clock one 60 Hz period per pump, and L58's window-count assertion catches any pump that executes two ticks and skips a read.
duelRules.ts:L35: rules.tick(s) is s.duel.interior.tick, the value the test samples.
Other journal resets (core.ts:L427 controls >= 256 on lifecycle; L478 frames > 4096) are not plausibly reached within one 300-tick window of this scripted round with no pauses.
duelProducers.ts:L54-72: the results loop still runs before the paused check, the retry sequence (max of commandHighWater+1 and lastSequence+1) is unchanged, and no new path issues a pause.
duelClient.ts:L21-27: the identity checks run before validateDuelSnapshot, so a mismatched publication is rejected before it reaches the replica.
not_verified: I did not run the test suite (constraint), so I cannot confirm the new producer test fails without the fix except by reading the code path, or that the ten seeds still pass with the new window and heldHighWater assertions.
R1-F5 (a replica replacement validates twice) was deferred and not awaited; I did not re-examine it.

A possible race that predates this fix and was not introduced by it: a presence result applied in the pump just before a player's pause makes the steward issue pause('peer-lost') while the authority is already pausing. I did not trace the lifecycle queue to see whether this produces a visible second pause.
